Arachidonic acid metabolism emerged as the primary cross-paradigm winner: Mummichog (m/z-direct, empirical-compound network) ranked it #1 with p=0.0219, driven by leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909, ChEBI:15651), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG ORA independently ranked its KEGG ortholog (KEGG:hsa00590, Arachidonic acid metabolism) at rank 2 with p=0.0807, also centred on leukotriene A4. The convergent leukotriene A4 signal points to upstream 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) activity: LTA4 is the unstable epoxide intermediate from arachidonic acid that is hydrolysed to LTB4 or conjugated with glutathione to LTC4, driving leukotriene metabolism (MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism, also rank 2 in Mummichog). A secondary axis centred on norepinephrine (KEGG:C00547, ChEBI:18357) emerged across both Mummichog tyrosine-metabolism (rank 3, p=0.0219) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG:hsa00350 (rank 1, p=0.0771); RaMP ORA anchored this in the broader Reactome GPCR and G-alpha-i signalling axis (REACT:R-HSA-418594, FDR=0.0016), where coumarin (KEGG:C05851, ChEBI:28794) also contributed. Coumarin additionally surfaced as a solo hit in Mummichog xenobiotics metabolism (rank 5, p=0.0325), consistent with its known role as a CYP2A6 substrate. Methimazole (ChEBI:50673, thionamide antithyroid), benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (ChEBI:30614, PAH DNA-adduct-forming carcinogen), N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (ChEBI:1784, aromatic amine), beta-mercaptoethanol (ChEBI:41218, antioxidant) and bromide (ChEBI:15858, halide ion) were either unresolved or produced no significant pathway hits, suggesting they are contextual outliers or present below detection thresholds for ORA. The biological narrative is therefore two-layered: (1) an inflammatory lipid mediator shift implicating leukotriene biosynthesis via 5-lipoxygenase, and (2) a neuroactive catecholamine axis implicating GPCR/alpha-2 adrenergic signalling with coumarin as a xenobiotic co-hit.

RaMP ORA ranked "G alpha (i) signalling events" (REACT:R-HSA-418594) first with FDR=0.0016, anchored by norepinephrine and coumarin. Downstream Reactome children included "GPCR downstream signalling" (REACT:R-HSA-388396), "GPCR ligand binding" (REACT:R-HSA-500792), and "Adrenaline signalling through Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor" (REACT:R-HSA-392023), collectively implicating the GPCR/G-alpha-i axis. The second layer centred on arachidonic acid: mummichog ranked "Arachidonic acid metabolism" (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) and "Leukotriene metabolism" (MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism) co-first at p=0.0206 with leukotriene A4 as the shared signal; MetaboAnalystR KEGG independently returned hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) at p=0.0807 with the same hit. Mummichog also recovered "Tyrosine metabolism" (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, p=0.0206) with norepinephrine and "Xenobiotics metabolism" (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism, p=0.0302) with coumarin as a co-signal. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies two perturbed axes: a GPCR/G-alpha-i neuroactive axis driven by norepinephrine and coumarin, and an inflammatory lipid-mediator axis driven by leukotriene A4.
